name: Trade war & tariffs
summary: China extended its rare-earth control pause and 24% tariff suspension to January on 9 Nov; truce stays short-term
state: On 9 Nov China extended its suspension of new rare-earth export controls to 10 Jan 2027, hours before the pause was due to lapse, and kept its suspension of a 24% tariff on US goods, leaving a 10% rate in place until January (Reuters via Internazionale; Bloomberg). The truce now runs for two months, with a Trump–Xi meeting expected at APEC in Shenzhen. Watch is kept with an easing trend.
for_you: Importers and firms using Chinese rare earths face another short deadline in January. Businesses can follow official guidance from the Department for Business and Trade on tariffs and export controls.
rubric_hit: Major US–China tariffs and controls suspended only to 10 Jan 2027 = Watch; no broad new tariffs with retaliation

sources.title: Internazionale (Reuters) — China extends suspension of new rare earth controls until January

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
